continuity_scope: Dungeons & Dragons Fourth Edition setting witness: Dark Sun Campaign Setting, Wizards of the Coast hardcover, 17 August 2010, ISBN 9780786954933. This is the 4e Athas setting-product continuity only, not the 1991/1995 TSR boxed-set continuities, novels, video games, fan material, or later core-D&D discussions.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Wizards of the Coast Fourth Edition hardcover, 17 August 2010, ISBN 9780786954933, 224 pages; contemporaneous publisher spring-catalog archive.
Wizards of the Coast Unearthed Arcana PDF (2016); Athas comparison/reference only, not a Dark Sun edition witness.

coverage_rule: Terms-only audit. The accessible official synopsis/catalogue material establishes a setting product, its world/region, environmental magic context, sorcerer-king political frame, and game options, but has no claim-level fixed named-character text. No character or relationship record is created. City-states, ancestries, classes, factions, sorcerer-kings as a category, psionics, artifacts, places, rules, and player characters remain terms, not nodes.
omissions: All named individuals, including individual sorcerer-kings, novel protagonists, adventure NPCs, and video-game characters; each needs a separate exact work/product witness with claim-level evidence.
The original 1991 TSR box, the 1995 revised setting, all novels/adventures, game adaptations, Athas.org/fan material, and any unspecified core-D&D treatment.
Defiling, preserving, individual gods, and other detailed rule/lore claims not directly exposed by the declared 4e synopsis archive.
Player characters, ancestries, classes, city-states, factions, artifacts, places, and generic monsters as character nodes.
uncertainties: The primary catalogue is an archive copy of a contemporaneous Wizards of the Coast catalog rather than a live first-party store page; exact product metadata and the quoted 4e synopsis are high confidence, but no fuller text is inferred.
The 2010 catalog expressly frames the book as an update of a classic setting for 4e, so it must not be used to silently reconcile earlier TSR or other continuities.
Dark Sun depictions include slavery, environmental collapse, coercive rule, and survival/arena violence. The audit records these only as non-graphic content cautions.
evidence_basis: The archived 2010 Wizards catalog gives the exact 4e product, date, ISBN, setting synopsis, Athas, sorcerer-kings, regions, and rules scope. A Wizards-hosted 2016 document identifies Athas as a Dark Sun world where psionics is common and magic is an ecological scourge. No wiki or fan-setting material is used.

citations.locator: 2010 Wizards of the Coast Spring Catalog, pp. 25-26
supports: Exact 4e product/date/ISBN and official synopsis of Athas, sorcerer-kings, regions, character options, and survival/arena/desert material.
